# OpenAI Interview Guide

> The whole OpenAI loop: process, coding, system design, behavioral, levels, and a question bank. A free guide from DesignGurus.io, in plain Markdown, with no account required.

Each page is short and ends with links to full course lessons and free articles. Each description below is the opening sentence of that page.

## Guide pages

- [The OpenAI behavioral interview](https://github.com/design-gurus/openai-interview-guide/blob/main/behavioral-interview.md): OpenAI is commonly reported to spread behavioral evaluation across the loop instead of holding one deciding culture round.
- [The OpenAI coding interview](https://github.com/design-gurus/openai-interview-guide/blob/main/coding-interview.md): The OpenAI coding round is commonly reported as a practical task, not an algorithm puzzle.
- [Common mistakes in the OpenAI interview](https://github.com/design-gurus/openai-interview-guide/blob/main/common-mistakes.md): The mistakes that candidates report most often in the OpenAI loop concern format, not knowledge.
- [A four-week plan for the OpenAI interview](https://github.com/design-gurus/openai-interview-guide/blob/main/four-week-plan.md): Four weeks is enough to prepare for the OpenAI loop if you already write code daily.
- [The OpenAI interview process](https://github.com/design-gurus/openai-interview-guide/blob/main/interview-process.md): The OpenAI engineering interview is commonly reported to run in five stages after the application.
- [OpenAI levels and how the interview changes by level](https://github.com/design-gurus/openai-interview-guide/blob/main/levels.md): Candidates report OpenAI engineering levels that run from L2 to L7.
- [OpenAI interview question bank](https://github.com/design-gurus/openai-interview-guide/blob/main/question-bank.md): This page lists 56 questions in three groups: 28 coding, 14 system design, and 14 behavioral.
- [How the OpenAI loop differs by role](https://github.com/design-gurus/openai-interview-guide/blob/main/roles.md): The shared parts of the OpenAI loop are coding, a project round, and behavioral conversations.
- [The OpenAI system design interview](https://github.com/design-gurus/openai-interview-guide/blob/main/system-design-interview.md): OpenAI asks system design, and depending on the role it asks twice: once as an early screen and again, in more depth, inside the final loop.

## Related free guides

- [Grokking System Design](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design): 30 patterns, 59 question walkthroughs, 35 cheat sheets, and guides for 122 companies.
- [Grokking Coding Interview](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview): The 41 coding patterns and how to recognize each one in a new problem.

- [API Design Interview](https://github.com/design-gurus/api-design-interview): A six-step method for the API design round, the core concepts, and eight question walkthroughs.

- [DevOps and SRE Interview](https://github.com/design-gurus/devops-sre-interview): The loop round by round: troubleshooting, Linux and networking, SRE system design, and incident response.

- [Solutions Architect Interview](https://github.com/design-gurus/solutions-architect-interview): Architecture design, customer discovery, and presentation rounds, with loops at five cloud and data companies.
- [Staff Engineer Interview](https://github.com/design-gurus/staff-engineer-interview): What changes at staff level: the loop, system design at staff scope, the project deep dive, and down-leveling.
- [Engineering Manager Interview](https://github.com/design-gurus/engineering-manager-interview): The manager loop round by round: people management, project retrospective, behavioral, and system design for managers.
- [Amazon Leadership Principles](https://github.com/design-gurus/amazon-leadership-principles): All 16 principles with interview questions, sample answers, and how the Amazon loop works.
- [Software Engineer Levels](https://github.com/design-gurus/software-engineer-levels): Engineering ladders at 17 companies, how levels map across them, and what interviews expect at each level.
